To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the inference network of a variational autoencoder is prone to lagging behind the true model posterior, and that this lagging can be reduced by aggressively optimizing the inference network during the early stages of training.

(1) VAEs are susceptible to posterior collapse during training, (2) posterior collapse can be avoided through aggressive optimization of the inference network, and (3) our approach outperformed strong autoregressive and variational baselines on text generation and image reconstruction tasks, and is competitive while being substantially faster.

(i) VAE training can be understood as an optimization process where the model's posterior is a moving target and inference lag can cause posterior collapse, and (ii) a simple modification to the training procedure can avoid collapse and improve performance on text and image data.
